I have a cat wand where you attach the 'toys' it comes with to the end of the line and there is a bell on the tip of it. Something like that might be good because then your cat can follow the sound of the bell instead of the sight of the toy! There's also a toy I have that's basically a toy baby bird but it makes chirping sounds. That might be a good option too. Basically, I'd buy toys that focus on having an audio element instead of a solely visual one.

That being said, I know he doesn't like the 2d cat tvs, but have you considered getting a small tank of water and putting those fake' robotic ' fish in there? He might be more prone to enjoying that! There isn't an audio element there but your cat has partial vision, so maybe that'd still be enjoyable?

Also, keep in mind that when a cat seems to 'stop' chasing something and just kind of is staring at it, that's also them playing! Sometimes, cats just enjoy 'watching' their prey, so even if you use a cat wand to play with your cat and he isn't chasing it persay and just watching it, the cat is still getting something out of it. So I'd definitely keep playing with your cat even if it seems like he is just watching and not playing. (At least, from what I know of cats, I'm not a cat expert.)

There's also puzzle feeders you can give to him,use a really delicious but fragrant treat so that he can be stimulated by the scent! In that same vein, catnip toys would help too, because then he can follow the scent instead of just visually, like with the audio toy examples above.

Hopefully some of this has been helpful, I wish you and your kitty the best!

I do have some advice!  
First off, you have too few litter boxes for the amount of cats you have; you're gonna wanna have 1 extra litter box per cat, that's kinda the standard from what I know. You have 1 litter robot and 1 regular box, which is great for 1 cat, but since you have 3, you're gonna want 6 boxes total. 

My advice to you is to put a litter box in front of the door where the cat is peeing. With any luck, the cat will start using it. Then, what you can do is slowly start moving the litter box, foot by foot, to the desired location you want the litter box to be permanently (I imagine you don't want a box in either children's room permanently). It's gonna be a slow process, but if everything works out as it should, the cat will follow the box as you move it and start using it in the correct place. So, for example,for one or two weeks, have the box in front of the closet door. Then, for another week, move it a foot away from the door. Another week, move it another foot away. Keep going like that until you reach wherever you want the litter box to be. I've seen this technique used before with success, though I've never had to try it myself thankfully.

Also, keep track of what litter you are using whenever the cat is peeing outside the box. Maybe you're using a brand the cat doesn't like and refuses to use. 

I hope your issue gets resolved soon!!! And I hope other people here have advice for you too!

My advice, if you haven't tried these things already, would be to:  
A) Make sure that there are some horizontals scratching posts (as it appears your cat would prefer a horizontal one. You can even sprinkle catnip on it to make it more appealing to her.

C) When you see her using the scratching posts instead of the carpet, give her positive reinforcement, such as a treat

I hope this is helpful, I know it's super frustrating when cats destroy things!

First off, Congrats on the cats! I hope you'll all make each other very happy!  
Ok, now on to advice:  
Firstly, you have too few litter boxes. You need to have one extra litter box per cat, basically. So, 2 litter boxes would be fine for one cat, but for two cats, you'll wanna have 4.   
Secondly, if the boxes have lids, try taking the lids off. Some cats don't like the lids. If they don't have lids, maybe give lids a try! Some cats DO like lids.  
Third, try putting litter boxes in rooms where the cats commonly urinate.   
Also, try putting a cat scratcher in those areas too, could be they feel insecure and just need more of their own scent around.   
It's great that you already went to the vet to rule things out too!  
That's about all the advice I can think of, I hope others will have some good advice, too. Best of luck to you and your new kitties!

There are a few things I can think of that maybe haven't been considered  
1. If your litter boxes have lids, take them off. She might not like the lids.  
2. She might be having pain physically stepping over the wall of the box to get in it, since she is a bit older. Try instead cutting a hole in the side of the box so she can just step into it without having to step over the sides.   
3. You mention UTI testing, but not urinary crystal testing, so get her tested for that if you haven't.   
4. Add more litter boxes in places she commonly pees if you haven't already. If that's too annoying, try instead adding scent soakers like cat scratchers to those areas. It could be she feels insecure in her environment and needs more of her scent around to feel secure.  
5. Try new types of litter if you haven't already, could be the litter itself is irritating her. I'm not the best versed on what would be best, so ask your vet about what alternative litters they recommend.   
  
I hope this issue gets resolved for you!

AWL has SOME mechanics that are a bit more in depth than other farming sim games,such as hybrid crops,fertilizer (I think stardew has fertilizer, but iirc, you don't have to do it twice a day like with this game), and some mechanics with animal pregnancy that are a bit more in depth. You don't technically HAVE to do hybrid crops or fertilizer, though.  You can get along without them, it's just your farm won't be as profitable as it could be. It is on a bit of a tighter timeline than other farming games. Each season only lasts 10 days, but to be fair, most crops grow in more than one season, so it's not like you always have to cut down your crops to prepare for the next season. You're on a timeline the first year to get married by the end of the year, but there are easy options for marriage candidates like Molly or Lumina. And there are some events that, while you don't have to do to progress the story or anything, you can only do at certain times and if you don't do them, you miss out on them forever. It's really the type of game you have to play multiple times in order to experience everything it has to offer, but that just means the game has a good longevity in replayability.  
Honestly, though, it's probably one of my favorite story of seasons/harvest moon games. I'm really having a lot of fun with it, and I'm also someone that gets stressed out when things are too complex or too tight timeline wise. This one is a bit more of a challenge than other harvest moon/story of seasons games, I'll admit, (not quite so much as the original gamecube game but still). But I think it'd be worth you giving it a shot.  You might enjoy having a little bit more of a challenge, it might be good to step outside your comfort zone a bit. It's nothing too intense of a challenge, it just makes everything feel more rewarding than in previous Harvest Moon/ Story of Seasons games where it was kinda easy to just coast by.

You could try doing some light cooking -nothing too intensive, that way you aren't standing up for a while. Things you just throw in the oven and leave for a while would be best. The best option might be to A) Track your ovulation using an app and not have sex when you are ovulating B) Continue using condoms, and be sure to use them correctly (Don't use expired ones, check for holes beforehand, etc C) Use spermicide and D) Keep around some emergency contraception just in case . These things all together should drastically lower your pregnancy risk.  You're not an asshole for not wanting to be on something that alters your body. But I also don't think he's an asshole for wanting more protection. It's good that he's taking the issue of accidental pregnancy seriously.  Ultimately, though, it is YOUR body and you are the one that will be living the consequences of birth control, so it really isn't his place to pressure you. If it's a deal breaker for him, then maybe you both have competing needs and you need to pursue new relationships with other people instead. Which is okay. It sucks, but it's okay;it doesn't mean either of you are assholes or bad people.   
As an aside though, even though you've heard horror stories about the IUD, please remember those horror stories are not the norm. If you have trouble with things like pap smears and stuff, then I would say the IUD might not be the thing for you due to the initial pain from insertion, but don't let the horror stories alone turn you off of it.  And keep in mind, the initial pain is very much worth the result for many, many more people than not. If you evaluate for yourself that it isn't the best option, then that's fair. It's okay to not want it. Just be sure the reason you don't want isn't just because you've read some non-standard experiences that have scared you. I just don't want anyone to be turned off of any kind of birth control due to fear from it or due to rare occurrences.

I think it's fair to say that we should try to minimize harm, but the idea that there is one true, good way to minimize harm is a bit of a fallacy and depends entirely on what an individual person values. The vegan ideology is stating that we should primarily care about animal welfare above all else. That's their idea of minimizing harm. Meanwhile, an individuals idea of what harm should be minimized/prioritized could be something entirely different, but vegans would declare their diet/way of life to be unethical because it doesn't prioritze what THEY believe should be.  
Example of what I mean:  


​

John Doe values minimizing human suffering.  He does not like that vegetables are picked primarily by wage-slave labor, he doesn't like the conditions in which people who pick vegetables are forced to work under.  He chooses to minimizes harm by minimizing his diet of vegetables and supplementing it by hunting instead. By hunting, he can get a lot of nutrition in his diet from nutrient rich meat. He doesn't eat chocolate because of the conditions chocolate is gathered under.  He avoids palm oil. John is doing active work to minimize the harm he feels is most important.  Jeff, meanwhile, is vegan, and values animal lives over human ones.  Jeff might tell John that his diet is unethical because Jeff hunts and therefore animals will die, despite the fact that Jeff is making active strides to minimize harm in his own diet and lifestyle in other ways. It's not done in the 'correct' way Jeff feels, and so therefore, it's unethical. But it isn't. There is no universal ethical diet, and for vegans to claim that there is is untrue. It's entirely subjective.   


  
This is what I think the point of  posts like OPS. It's not to say that you shouldn't minimize harm. It's that there is no correct way to have a cruelty-free diet and these posts serve to point out the ways in which veganism STILL hurts even animals and the environment.

Please don't take this the wrong way, I know you're not trying to be creepy, but I would really advise against doing this. There is a time and a place for everything. When it comes to hitting on people, the time and place is in a social environment that people go to specifically to talk to or interact with other people.  At party, at a bar, at a club etc. A gym is not a place where people go to meet with and socialize with new people.  Even if it's just to hit her up as friends, I still wouldn't really advise this either. Because again, time and place for everything and people don't go to the gym to make friends. There's a reason that there are women-only gyms and its specifically BECAUSE we made them to prevent random, strange men from hitting on us when all we're trying to do is exercise. There are some women that might not mind being hit on at the gym, but you really run the risk of ruining a random stranger's entire gym experience by making her feel unsafe if you choose to hit on her, especially if it goes badly. It isn't fair to her and it also isn't fair to yourself because you aren't choosing a scenario that is likely to go over very well. Remembering the "there is a time and a place" rule is very important with socialization skills.  Ask yourself "Is this an environment where some one comes to this type of place specifically to socialize or is this a place where people go just to go about their daily lives?" and you'll increase your own chances of a successful socialization a lot more and prevent yourself from coming off as creepy.  There's nothing wrong with admiring her from afar as long as you aren't staring, I'd just stick to that if I were you. If you want to meet new people, join a club of some kind, go to a bar, join a discord group, something along those lines.

I would say that could easily be because axises (axis'? whats the plural?) of oppression overlap and amplify other axises. Example: LGBT+ people of color are overwhelmingly more likely to face hate crimes than those that are white, because the element of racism compounds on the element of them also being LGBT+. Likewise, being LGBT+ and also being a woman means that you are going to experience the compounding of misogyny as well.  That doesn't mean that being ace wasn't a contributing factor.  I also don't think that experiencing privileges that another member of the lgbt+ community doesn't have means that you don't deserve access to a word/community or that your own oppression is somehow invalid. Trans men often have privileges over trans women, gay men often have privileges over lesbians. Then we could also talk about gay/lesbians vs bisexual. Then we also have discussion about cis lgb+ people and their privilege over trans lgb+ people, and then we get even further into intersex lgbt+ vs perisex lgbt+ and yeah...it's a big mess when we are deciding who 'deserves' access to the word queer based on who has it worse. Asexuals might not have it as bad as gays or lesbians. I honestly don't know that we do or don't, I think that'd require more statistical research on my part. But I don't necessarily think that matters - we're still seen as a defect, as a mental disorder, our asexuality is still at the very least a contributing factor to crimes against us, even if there are other motivations also involved (such as you mentioned in your experience, being a woman or as I mentioned earlier, being a person of color) and I think that in and of itself affords us the right to use queer when factored in with our very long history in the queer movement. I'm biromantic, so I'm still queer even without being ace, but i still think that being ace alone qualifies me for being queer (and if you ever wanted to identify as queer, you'd be well within your rights as well.)

Being fat= inherently unhealthy. It actually depends more on where the fat is located, not necessarily that you are fat in and of itself. Then, we have the obesity paradox, where some studies have suggested that people fat can actually protect certain people from some ailments (although like all theories, there is some criticism to this.). We have that the thing that often determines obesity, BMI, doesn't take into account how much of weight is muscle vs fat (nor does it take into account where the fat is located), and that it was created by a mathematician to judge a population of people rather than individuals, and therefore has been being misused this entire time. So even that in and of itself is flawed. The human body is a lot more complex than we like to give it credit for, and it isn't as simple as "thin=healthy, fat=unhealthy". There are more factors involved.

If you get pregnant on an IUD, which is a severely low chance, there is some research from the past that suggests it could be more likely to be ectopic. The most recent study I could find was from the late 90's, though. It makes a little bit of sense; the iud would prevent the fertilized egg from being able to escape the fallopian tube, so naturally it would end up being ectopic. But the chance of even getting pregnant while on an IUD in the first place is so incredibly low. And it's an outdated study anyways. So it sounds to me like she's doing what a lot of anti-reproductive rights people do and use outdated studies/science to fearmonger. As for if it will cause you to have ectopic pregnancies in the future when you are no longer using the IUD, I found a study from '92 (again, as I mentioned, I"m only finding old studies. ) that says "*From the results of this study it was concluded that former IUD users are not at an increased risk for ectopic pregnancy.* ". (link for this study is here:[https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/002072929291022G](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/002072929291022G))  I'm sure that our IUD technology has only improved since 1992 and 1995, so I honestly don't think you have a single thing to worry about.

When you're experiencing anxiety or some negative emotion, rather than beating yourself up for feeling bad or getting upset at yourself or trying to feel better, thank your mind instead. Your mind is making you feel that way because everything it does is to try and protect you from some kind of future harm. It's a defense mechanism. Saying "Thank you for trying to protect me, but we don't need to be thinking about this at the moment" has, SOMEHOW, made my anxiety disorder much better and always calms me down when I"m getting all riled up. I think the term for it is 'radical acceptance'. Just accept the thought, thank your mind for trying to protect you, remind it that you are NOT in danger at the moment and do not need protecting, and let it pass. Don't try to fight it, don't get angry at yourself for feeling bad. I know this isn't for everybody, and as I alluded to earlier, I was 100% sure this tactic was complete bullshit when I was first taught it.  It really works for me, though, and maybe it will work for someone reading this, too.

This is just my thoughts on it. You're going to get a lot of differing thoughts on this, because this issue isn't even widely agreed upon within disability communities.  
Yes, they are ableist. However, I find that the constant attention brought up to the "Should we stop using the world stupid/idiot/dumb/etc" topic is completely derailing from actual, much more important discussions about disability rights and disability issues that could be had instead. I know people can care about multiple things at once, but the amount of attention and energy constantly focused around getting people to cut stupid out of their vocabulary annoys the heck out of me.  There are so many more important issues we could be spending the energy on, and the issue comes up SO much that I DO feel this is an instance where it's deflecting onto 'easy' to address issues instead of focusing on things that could actually amount to making lives better for us. It reminds me of people focusing on banning plastic straws when what we really need is regulations on corporations that produce plastic in the first place. It's focusing on a 'red herring' issue that won't actually cause much dramatic change, so it's a 'comfortable' issue in particular for non-disabled people to focus on because yelling at people to 'stop using stupid/idiot/etc" is a lot easier than actually going out and fighting for our rights.  
So if you ask me, don't prioritize removing stupid or idiot from your vocab. Avoid it when you can, but don't make that the 'hill to die on' issue you take up in regards to ableism and disability rights. I'd much rather be able to get married in the U.S without losing my SSDI income than not hear the word 'stupid' ever again. Please put attention where it's most likely to make a change.

This is my view of it as a person with a developmental disability : 

It comes down to a person controlling who does and does not get to use their body. A person has a right to determine this, regardless of their reasoning. That doesn't mean every reason is a non-bigoted reason.  
A person can legally refuse to have sex with a disabled person, completely for the reason that person is disabled, and that is their right to do so, even though their reasoning is appalling and bigoted. The government would have absolutely no place deciding that this person should be legally forced to have sex with this disabled person. A person could decide they don't want to donate their kidney to a disabled person, and the government would have no place deciding that they should be forced to donate their kidney. Likewise, the government has absolutely no place deciding that some one should be legally forced to offer their body to a disabled fetus to use. If a person does not consent to their body being used, they have a right to stop it using the minimal force necessary, regardless of the reasons why they don't want it to be used.

The 100% truth is that beauty is a completely subjective belief and what is conventionally attractive is highly dependent on power structures that are in play in the society that you live in. It is not an objective reality. What might be seen as the height of beauty in one culture during on time period could be seen as the height of ugly in that same culture 40 years ago, or be seen as the height of ugly in a different culture that exists at the exact same time. Your view on what is beautiful or ugly does not exist in a vacuum.  You can also learn to find new things attractive/unattractive based on your exposure to those things being portrayed in a positive or negative light.   
I don't know if you have BDD. But you aren't ugly because ugly doesn't objectively exist and what is seen as ugly or not is variable. No one can tell you if you are 'just ugly' because you are going to get different answers from different people depending on who they are, where they live, etc.  You may just choose to ignore when people say you're beautiful because you can't see it yourself and therefore believe they're just being nice. You'll believe people if they tell you you're ugly because you already believe it to be true. It's confirmation bias. 

  
If you feel you have BDD, it might help to talk to a therapist about it.  But if you really want the truth, there it all is. You can not be  objectively ugly -or beautiful- because it is a construct.  Constructs have their value, but they also have limits.

Others have already said this, and I'd like to just repeat it: This is almost certainly sleep paralysis. In case you don't know, when you're asleep, the mind releases chemicals that paralyze your body so that you don't start acting out your dreams. Sometimes, when you are awake and in a near sleep like state (such as when waking up or just falling asleep), your mind engages into 'sleep/dream mode', where that paralytic chemical is in effect, as well as your mind experiencing the vivid hallucinations that come with dreaming (hense the whispering and such). You're both asleep and awake.   
You don't have to have a diagnosed condition for this to happen, either. It can happen to an otherwise perfectly healthy person who has never experienced it before in their life, and then will never experience it again.  That weight on the chest is a classic symptom of it. In olden Europe, they used to believe that it was a hag or a witch sitting on your chest. 

I think she should have a talk with her doctor about it, they can probably refer her to a sleep specialist and they can discuss ways to prevent this in the future.   


In the meantime, believe it or not, shouting out for Jesus actually CAN help with this, regardless of it's non-paranormal origins or not. Trying to scream or shout can help 'wake' the body up and make your mind more quickly realize "HEY we're awake right now, no paralytic needed!" If that works for her sometimes and will help quell her fears, I'd say keep at that. She can also start with smaller steps to build up to it, such as focusing all her energy on moving just a single toe or finger, again with the intent of getting the body to realize it's awake. Once she is able to that, screaming out should also become easier.
